newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Jardine sees lower profit for 1996 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Jardine sees lower profit for 1996 - paper.

text.p: Jardine Matheson Holdings' trading profit for 1996 was not expected to match that of 1995, the Business Times said on Tuesday.
The newspaper said Jardine's group finance director Chris Cowan blamed the expected slump in profit partly on retail company Dairy Farm's worse performance.

"The outlook for Dairy Farm was much worse than we had anticipated, and higher level of start-up costs affected both Dairy Farm and Jardine Pacific...and in the life assurance business, investment income was hit (as) the Thai stock market has fallen out," Cowan was quoted as telling Singapore
Dairy Farm last month reported a 39 percent and 55 percent fall respectively in trading profits to US$53 million and net earnings to US$28 million.

Cowan said Dairy Fram incurred repositioning costs in changing the format of its Sizzler restaurants, and in Franklins supermarket which is switching its strategy from a dry grocer to a fresh food supermarket chain.
Better results from JIB Group, Jardine Fleming, Hongkong Land, Mandarin Oriental and Cycle & Carriage offset declines in Jardine Pacific, Jardine International Motors and Dairy Farm.
Jardine Fleming was making a provision of US$20 million due to a recent trading scandal, half of which would be borne by Jardine Matheson, the Business Times said.
Jardine Matheson reported a 17 percent fall in net profit to US$213 million for the first half ended June 30.
